content.text: Ayurveda has a strong presence and roots in Maharashtra, particularly in areas like Pune and Mumbai. Here, a large number of Ayurvedic colleges exist, and the demand for Ayurveda is increasing day by day. BAMS course, also known as Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery, is now available at 132 colleges in Maharashtra. It is a 5.5-year program that includes 1 year of on-field internship. The National Eligibility cum Entrance test(NEET UG) is necessary for BAMS admission in Maharashtra.

In this article, we are going to cover the important information regarding eligibility, fees, top colleges, and the procedure for taking BAMS admission in colleges of Maharashtra. Follow this article minutely to get an overall idea about the BAMS admission in Maharashtra.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission in Maharashtra Key Highlights

content.text: To take admission to the BAMS course, a student must qualify NEET and attend the Maharashtra Ayush Counselling . The Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell (CET Cell) and AYUSH Admissions Central Counselling Committee (AACCC) are responsible for conducting the counselling procedure to solicit students for BAMS admission in Maharashtra. There are a total of 5289 BAMS seats in Maharashtra; among them, 438 are government seats and 4851 are private seats. The total government BAMS seat in Maharashtra is lower, considering the competition behind them.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Maharashtra

content.text: BAMS admission process in Maharashtra is done through the AYUSH counselling. Below is the step-by-step guide to the counselling procedure.
Step 1: Appear in the NEET UG examination of that concluding year. Score a promising mark in that examination to get a higher chance of admission to the BAMS course.
Step 2: Once NTA releases the results of NEET, check for your NEET marks and compare them with the NEET cut-off marks of that year. (Each year, the cut-off marks varied from the previous year)

Step 3: Register for the Maharashtra State Counselling on their official website. Upload the necessary documents that are required at the time of registration. Double-check your verification email for registration confirmation.
Step 4: After registration, candidates must fill in their preferred colleges and courses. The CET Cell uses a merit-based system to allot seats, considering NEET ranks and preferences.
Step 5: Once the seat allotment results are published online, check for your application status. Find which seats you are allotted.
Step 6: Next, the candidate must report to their college for document verification. Carry all of the prescribed documents, both in originals and photocopies.
Step 7: Lastly, pay the admission fees to confirm your seats.

Follow all these steps. If students are not allotted seats in the first round of counselling, wait for the next rounds. Each round fills the vacant seats that remain not allotted till the end of the counselling session.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for BAMS Admission in Maharashtra

content.text: There is a set of eligibility criteria for BAMS admission in Maharashtra. Students must comply with these criteria to get a chance for admission to the BAMS course. The crtiera are mentioned below.

items: Candidates must have completed 10+2 or equivalent from a recognised board with physics, chemistry, and biology (PCB) as mandatory subjects.
A minimum aggregate of 50% in PCB is required for general category students, while reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC) need at least 40% to 45%, depending on the college and state norms.
English is also a compulsory subject in Class 12.
Applicants must be at least 17 years old as of December 31 of the admission year. There is no upper age limit for NEET-based admissions.
Students must qualify the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET).

sections.heading: Documents Required for BAMS Admission in Maharashtra

content.text: Both uploading of the documents at the time of registration and document verification are necessary for admission. Failing to produce a single one of them may result in the cancellation of the candidature. The set of documents required for BAMS admission in Maharashtra is as follows.

items: The NEET Scorecard
The NEET Registration Form
Birth Certificate
Caste Certificate (other than general)
Income Certificate
Domicile Certificate
Class 10th & 12th Marksheet and Certificate
Migration Certificate
Transfer Certificate
Passport size photos, same as NEET application (6)
Allotment Letter
Gap Affidavit
Any Government Photo Identity Proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Voter Card, etc.)

sections.heading: Top BAMS Colleges in Maharashtra

content.text: The highest number of BAMS colleges exists in Maharashtra. Students get the option to choose from a variety of colleges to take admission. There are a total of 132 BAMS colleges in Maharashtra . Among them, 11 are Government and Government-aided colleges. And the rest 121 are private and private deemed colleges. Those 11 colleges provide 438 BAMS seats, and the 121 private colleges have 4851 seats for BAMS admission.

sections.heading: BAMS Course Fees in Maharashtra

content.text: BAMS course fees in Maharashtra are decided by the college. It is jointly agreed on by the Ministry of AYUSH and the Government of India. So, all the government and private colleges of the state have different BAMS course fees.

The private ones have higher course fees than the government ones. They promise modern infrastructure and trained faculty, which will help the peers positively. Please visit the official websites of the colleges to get a detailed fee structure of the BAMS course. Generally, the candidates must pay the first year’s payment at the time of seat allotment and in instalments at the start of each year; they can pay the remaining fees.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
What are the eligibility criteria for BAMS admission in Maharashtra?

content.text: BAMS eligibility in Maharashtra is similar to other states. Students must pass the 12th with a 50% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/Biochemistry. Also should have to qualify NEET UG. They must be over the age of 17.

sections.heading: Who conducts Maharashtra BAMS counselling?

content.text: Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell (CET Cell) and AYUSH Admissions Central Counselling Committee (AACCC) jointly conduct Maharashtra BAMS counselling.

sections.heading: What are the BAMS course fees in Maharashtra?

content.text: As colleges decide the course fees, it differs from government to private colleges. While in government colleges, the fees stand between INR 45k to INR 1 Lac, the private colleges charge between 3 to 7 lac.

sections.heading: How to get admission in Maharashtra BAMS?

content.text: To get admission in BAMS in Maharashtra, the candidates must qualify NEET and participate in the counselling session, conducted by Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell.

sections.heading: What are the total BAMS seats in Maharashtra?

content.text: In total, there are 5289 BAMS seats in Maharashtra. Among them, 438 are in government colleges and 4851 are in private colleges.

sections.heading: Can I apply BAMS without NEET?

content.text: No, you cannot study BAMS without qualifying NEET exam. National Eligibility cum Entrance Test is mandatory for BAMS admission in Maharashtra.

sections.heading: Which is No. 1 BAMS college in Maharashtra?

content.text: You can’t select a single college to be the best over others, as there are many good colleges for BAMS admission in Maharashtra. Still, many pundits select Dr. D.Y. Patil College of Ayurved and Research Centre, and Sumatibhai Shah Ayurved Mahavidyalay over others.

sections.heading: What are the PG courses after BAMS?

content.text: After BAMS, you can join for PG courses such as MD/MS (Ayurveda), which are offered in various specialisations.
